faqs.question: What is football match analysis?
faqs.answer: Football match analysis is the process of using footage, observations and data to understand what happened in a game. Pitchside focuses on making phone-recorded small-sided matches easier for players to review through supported stats and highlights.

Pitchside can support conversations about a match, but the launch product is centred on grassroots player stats, highlights, leaderboards and personal records. It should not be presented as a replacement for a professional tactical analyst.
faqs.question: Is Pitchside a coaching analysis platform?
Does the app calculate fitness or workload data?
faqs.answer: Not in the approved launch plan. Do not promise distance, speed, sprint or workload data on this page.
The final correction workflow must be shown in the product and documented before launch. Until it is confirmed, describe results as reviewable beta output rather than final verified statistics.

data.heroH1: Football match analysis for the people who were on the pitch.

contentBlocks.content: The review players actually have after a match
Most amateur analysis happens in fragments. Someone remembers the missed chance. A defender remembers the interception that started the winner. The keeper remembers three saves nobody else counted.
Video changes the conversation because the match is still there. Pitchside's job is to make that recording easier to use.
A useful review should answer four questions:

items: What happened? Start with the match result and supported events.
When did it happen? Connect important moments to the recording.
Who was involved? Review player contributions where identification is supported.
What do we keep? Save the stats, highlights and personal moments that matter beyond one night.

contentBlocks.content: Review the match, not a dashboard full of noise
Pitchside is not trying to turn every player into a performance analyst. The launch experience focuses on outputs a regular group can understand quickly:

items: Personal Clips on the Paid plan

contentBlocks.content: The current beta is testing supported football events such as goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles. Exact event availability should always match Product Status.
There are no launch promises here for distance, sprint load or xG. Those are different measurements, and xG sits on the future Paid roadmap.
A better ten-minute conversation after the game
Imagine opening the match page with the group after full-time.

You check the score and the moments Pitchside found. The keeper reviews the saves. The team checks the leaderboard. A player opens the clip behind a goal or assist. If something is wrong, the output should be reviewed rather than treated as unquestionable truth.
That is the outcome this page sells: less time scrubbing through the recording, more time discussing the football that happened.
Where the analysis comes from

The starting point is ordinary phone footage. Record from a stable, elevated position near halfway, using one phone where it covers the whole pitch clearly or two phones when the far side becomes too small.
After upload, Pitchside processes the video and organises the supported output for review. During private beta, upload and processing can currently take up to 45 minutes.
For the detailed workflow, visit football video analysis. For the recording setup, see how to record football matches.
Who gets the most value from this page
The regular 5-a-side group
You already play every week. Pitchside gives the games a history instead of starting from zero every Tuesday.
The 6-a-side or 7-a-side team
Roles are clearer, the pitch is larger and off-ball contributions are easier to forget. Footage and supported stats give the review more context.
The player who wants evidence
Personal Stats and available clips help keep a record of what happened, not just what the group remembers.
The organiser who cannot log everything live
The recording becomes the source. Nobody has to spend the full match tapping goals, tackles and saves into a phone.
What Pitchside may get wrong
AI-assisted football match analysis is only as useful as the footage and the supported capability behind it.

items: Similar kits can make player identification harder.
Fencing, substitutes and spectators can block the view.
A low or distant phone angle can hide the ball and player actions.
Supported events may be assigned incorrectly and should be reviewed.

contentBlocks.content: Pitchside is in private beta because these cases need testing. The product should show uncertainty and allow review rather than present every result as perfect.

Plans for how often you review a match
The Free plan gives a player or group one recording per month with Match Stats & Highlights, Leaderboards and Personal Stats.
The Paid plan increases the allowance to one recording per week and adds Personal Clips. It costs £4.99 weekly, £12.99 monthly or £99 annually.
